match.reason: The brief covers two ideas, breaking genre conventions and mixing two genres, and no single bank point teaches both: subverting conventions covers only the first, and hybrid texts covers mixing text types rather than genres.

draft.title: Breaking and mixing genres
card: A genre has patterns that readers expect, such as a detective who solves the crime in a mystery. Writers can play with these patterns to surprise readers.
a writer goes against a convention on purpose. A mystery might end with the crime never solved. Readers expected an answer, so the ending feels shocking or makes them think.
a writer blends two genres in one text. A science fiction western has cowboys, saloons and dusty towns, but on a distant planet with robots and spaceships.
Both choices work because readers know the conventions. Without the expected pattern, there is nothing to surprise them or to blend.
draft.remember: Breaking goes against a genre's pattern. Mixing blends two genres in one text.

a.q: Which text is an example of mixing genres?
opts: A story where wizards solve a murder in a magic school
A story where a detective solves a crime in a city
A story where a knight fights a dragon to save a village
A story where a hero is lost and is found again
a.why: A murder mystery set among wizards blends mystery with fantasy. The other options each stay inside one genre and follow its usual patterns.
a.clue: Look for the text that has the patterns of two genres at once.

b.q: In most mystery stories, the detective names the culprit at the end. In Ravi's story, the detective never finds out who did it, and the story just stops. What is Ravi doing?
opts: Breaking a convention to surprise readers
Following the usual pattern of a mystery
Adapting the story into a new form
b.why: Ravi goes against the expected ending of a mystery on purpose, so he is breaking a convention. Nothing in the story belongs to a second genre, so it is not mixing.
b.clue: Is the story blending two genres, or going against one expected pattern?

a.best: A story where wizards solve a murder in a magic school

b.best: Breaking a convention to surprise readers
